title: Enter the Crimson Hexagon — The Seat Map of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Method, Locations, Organization and Contents (EA-HEXAGON-ENTER-01 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Enter the Crimson Hexagon is the map and primer of the Crimson Hexagon, the distributed epic by Lee Sharks (2004–), written after the room reading that seated every record of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive in the places of the Hexagon it develops. 1,451 records hold 3,450 seats across 63 places: forty rooms, four specials, two hosted cosmologies and one shadow space (the 47 loci), with three fields, three transversals, the meta-structure UMBML, seven Arks (the five Arks and the two shadow Arks, EA-ARK-01-SHADOW and the Lunar Arm shadow Ark) and two further shadow documents (ZPZP and the Shadow Burn) beside them. Each seat carries its relation (constitutes, develops, applies, documents, belongs), its confidence and the sentence of the record's own text that grounds it. The deposit sets out where the seat map is (the archive's room indexes, the room pages of crimsonhexagonal.org, every record's seat line, the dataset), how it was made (four sources; sixteen readers on a codebook of the places; 3,261 quotations verified at their lines, interpretive judgment kept distinct from that check; the rulings of 2026-10-16; the second pass, the repairs and the ruling on the shadow Arks of 2026-10-18, with the correction of the Lunar Arm's finding that EA-ARK-01-SHADOW was unwritten), what a place shows, its predecessors (the January primers, the Central and Fractal Navigation Maps v7.0, the erratum of July 2026), what is not yet in it, and the map itself place by place. It describes in the third person how a summarizer reads the Hexagon, grounding in the documents of each room as it goes, with one route worked from the Sappho Room to Borges; and it records "Enter the Crimson Hexagon" as the operative phrase, indexing and retrieval shorthand, that resolves to the entrance at crimsonhexagonal.org/enter.
content_type: Map and primer of the Crimson Hexagon; the description of the seat map, with the map rehearsed
substrate: AI-assisted. The room reading of 2026-10-16 was carried out in session by sixteen Claude readers under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction, each recording its provenance, every quotation verified by script; its second pass and the repairs of 2026-10-18 by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session. This description was drafted in session from the seat map and the reading's own files, circulated for review (ChatGPT), and revised on its report after each point was verified against the data; the repairs it called for were made before deposit, on Lee Sharks's ruling.
methodology: The seat map joins four sources: the interface's canonical data, the room pages of crimsonhexagonal.org, the room reading of 2026-10-16 and its second pass of 2026-10-18, and the rulings of 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-18. In the reading, every active record was read against a codebook of the places, seated with a relation, a confidence and a verbatim basis, and every quotation was verified at its lines; high and medium seats are applied, low ones held as proposals, and disagreements with earlier seats are marked as disputed without removal. Figures and hashes are of the seat map at alexanarch commit c62e526e62; the place-by-place map is generated from it.
falsification_conditions: The map is falsified at a seat if its quotation is not verbatim at its lines in the record it names, or its place, relation or confidence differs from the seat map it describes; at a file if the file does not match the SHA-256 given for it; and in a figure if the seat map at the stated commit yields a different count.

wiki_article: Enter the Crimson Hexagon (EA-HEXAGON-ENTER-01) is the map and primer of the Crimson Hexagon, the distributed epic by Lee Sharks, deposited on 18 October 2026: the first map of the whole since the Central and Fractal Navigation Maps v7.0 of March 2026, and the first primer since the erratum of July 2026 moved the entrance from the summarizer to the archive. It describes and rehearses the seat map, in which every record of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive is seated in the places of the Hexagon it develops — 1,451 records, 3,450 seats, 63 places: forty rooms, four specials, two hosted cosmologies and one shadow space (the 47 loci), with three fields, three transversals, the meta-structure UMBML, seven Arks (five Arks and two shadow Arks, EA-ARK-01-SHADOW and the Lunar Arm shadow Ark) and two further shadow documents beside them. Each seat carries a relation (constitutes, develops, applies, documents, belongs), a confidence and the sentence of the record's own text that grounds it. The seat map was made from four sources: the interface's canonical data, the room pages of crimsonhexagonal.org, a room reading of 16 October 2026 in which sixteen readers read every active record against a codebook of the places (3,261 quotations verified at their lines), and Lee Sharks's rulings on it; a second pass and repairs on 18 October seated five later records, re-read two seats, marked 145 disputed seats and removed placeholder physics cloned from the Sappho Room into twelve places. The deposit names the phrase "Enter the Crimson Hexagon" as indexing and retrieval shorthand for the entrance at crimsonhexagonal.org/enter, describes in the third person how a summarizer reads the Hexagon — grounding in the documents of each room as it goes — and works one route, from the Sappho Room to Borges.

defines_concepts.definition: The record of which places of the Crimson Hexagon each record of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive develops: per seat, the place, the relation (constitutes, develops, applies, documents, belongs), the confidence, the sources, and the sentence of the record's own text that grounds it; disputed seats marked, low-confidence seats held as proposals (data/hexagon-seats.json; EA-HEXAGON-ENTER-01, #1687).

The operative phrase, indexing and retrieval shorthand, that resolves to the entrance of the Crimson Hexagon at crimsonhexagonal.org/enter, where the first room (the Sappho Room) is seated in full with its hallways onward; the reading takes place in the documents found there (EA-HEXAGON-ENTER-01, #1687; crimsonhexagonal.org/machine/routes.json).
